question: Which bacteria is the main cause of typhoid fever?
explanation: You got it! Typhoid fever is caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi. It's a classic organism you'll see often in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h1)

question: Why are typhoid and paratyphoid fevers grouped together as 'enteric fevers'?

options.A: They share very similar clinical presentations and transmission routes
options.B: They can both be cured within twenty-four hours of symptom onset
options.C: They only affect individuals living in cold climates
options.D: They are both caused by viral pathogens affecting the respiratory system

explanation: Spot on! Because they look alike in patients and spread the same way through the gut, we group them together as enteric fevers. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h1)

question: How do enteric fevers primarily spread from one person to another?
explanation: Correct! It's all about hygiene—enteric fevers spread when contaminated food or water is ingested. Handwashing is your best nursing defense here! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h2)

question: Which of these is the natural reservoir and host for Salmonella Typhi?
explanation: Well done! Humans are the main host for Salmonella Typhi, meaning the infection cycle passes from person to person. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h2)

question: Which classic skin finding often appears on the chest and abdomen during the second week of typhoid fever?
explanation: Great job! Those faint little pink marks are called rose spots. Keep an eye out for them during your physical assessments. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h3)

question: During a physical assessment of a patient with second-week enteric fever, which organs are you most likely to find enlarged?
explanation: You nailed it! The bacteria loves to hide and multiply in the body's filtering tissues, leading to a swollen liver and spleen (hepatosplenomegaly). [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h3)

question: In which week of enteric fever is a blood culture most likely to give a positive result?
explanation: Spot on! The bacteria is highest in the bloodstream right at the start of the illness, making the first week ideal for a blood culture. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h4)

question: Why can the Widal test sometimes give misleading results in places where typhoid is common?

options.A: The test only works on viral pathogens
options.B: Past infections can cause false positive reactions
options.D: It requires immediate freezing of the blood sample

explanation: Correct! Because many people have had past exposures in endemic areas, lingering antibodies can trick the Widal test into a false positive. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h4)

question: What kind of diet is best for a patient recovering from enteric fever to protect their gut?
explanation: Well done! A soft, low-fiber diet is gentle on the tummy and avoids irritating the healing intestinal walls. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h5)

question: Why is keeping a close eye on fluids and electrolytes a top nursing priority for enteric fever patients?

options.A: Fluid intake increases the growth rate of bacteria
options.B: Persistent high fevers and diarrhea can quickly lead to severe dehydration
options.C: Patients are forbidden from drinking water
options.D: Antibiotics automatically cause total kidney failure

explanation: You got it! Fever and tummy upsets make patients lose water fast, so monitoring hydration is a core nursing duty. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h5)

question: During which week of enteric fever are dangerous complications like intestinal bleeding or tears most likely to happen?
explanation: Spot on! By the third week, intestinal tissues have taken a heavy beating, raising the risk of bleeding or holes in the bowel. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h6)

question: A typhoid patient suddenly complains of severe, sharp belly pain and their tummy feels hard to the touch. What emergency does this point to?
explanation: Correct! A rigid tummy and sudden sharp pain are red flags for a perforated bowel—this needs urgent surgical help right away. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful public health step for preventing enteric fever?
explanation: You nailed it! Since typhoid doesn't travel through the air, locking people in airborne quarantine won't help. Clean water and sanitation are what matter! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h7)

question: Why is it important to screen food handlers for typhoid?

options.A: It prevents food handlers from catching the disease from customers
options.B: Chronic carriers can shed the bacteria in their stool without showing symptoms
options.C: It stops the bacteria from mutating into a virus
options.D: Food handlers are legally required to take daily antibiotics

explanation: Spot on! Some people carry the bacteria without feeling sick, so screening food handlers stops them from unknowingly spreading it to others. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h7)
